title: Stitch traces across Kafka batch jobs and worker pools
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We currently observe fragmented traces when requests traverse synchronous API servers, are enqueued to Kafka, processed by batched consumers and then fan out to worker pools. This results in orphaned spans in Jaeger/Tempo and makes end-to-end latency debugging and SLO attribution difficult.

Goal: Implement a robust trace-stitching strategy so spans originating in the request path and the asynchronous consumers/workers are correlated into single traces exported to our tracing backends (Tempo/Jaeger) via OTLP. The implementation should handle batch consumers (where multiple logical messages are processed in one consumer span), multiple worker retries, deduplication, and partial failures without causing large duplication of spans or blowing up sampling rates.

Scope and approach:
- Instrument Kafka producers to add a compact trace header (W3C traceparent + Redwood message-id) for out-of-band correlation.
- Update consumer libraries to extract trace context at batch boundaries, create a parent batch span, and then stitch per-message child spans inside the batch. For fan-out to worker pools, propagate the message-level trace info in the worker envelope and stitch worker spans as children.
- Add server-side span stitching in our trace pipeline: when a message-level span arrives without a matching parent (e.g., due to sampling), enrich the exported span with a synthetic parent marker that links to the originating request span using message-id metadata. This enrichment happens in the trace preprocessor before OTLP export.
- Ensure the exporter to Tempo/Jaeger preserves the reconstructed parent-child relationship and does not create cycles. Maintain idempotency: dedupe spans using message-id + span-id hashes for a configurable time window.
- Provide an opt-in rollout and feature flag per-tenant so we can test on internal services first.

Non-goals: Full rework of Kafka client libraries; this ticket will extend our in-house wrapper and add middleware hooks. Long-term sampling policy changes are separate (covered in another initiative).
acceptance_criteria: Kafka producers attach compact trace headers (traceparent + message-id) for instrumented services
Consumer batch span is created and per-message child spans are authored and linked in traces for instrumented consumers
Worker pool processing preserves message-level trace context and appears as children under the originating batch span in Tempo/Jaeger
Trace pipeline preprocessor can stitch orphaned message spans to originating request spans using message-id metadata in at least 80% of test scenarios
Span duplication rate due to stitching remains below 1% in canary traffic
E2E test harness simulates production-like batching and shows stable latency with stitching enabled (no >5% p99 regression),
Feature is behind a tenant-level feature flag and rollout plan exists (10% internal canary -> 50% -> 100%)
comments: 2025-01-08 - Maya Chen: Created ticket after on-call incident where three customer incidents were traced to missing correlation between API requests and async workers. Initial design doc linked.

2025-01-09 - Luca Romano: Implemented producer header injection and a prototype consumer middleware. Local tests show per-message spans being created inside batch consumer process. Opening PR for client changes.

2025-01-11 - SRE Review (Ana Torres): Concern about possible span explosion for high-throughput topics. Suggested dedupe window and a metrics counter for stitched vs orphan spans. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-01-13 - Design Review (Ravi Patel): UX for dashboards reviewed; proposed new Grafana panel to show orphaned span ratio and stitch success rate per topic and tenant. Linked dashboard prototype.

2025-01-14 - Luca Romano: Added trace preprocessor hook implementation and unit tests for synthetic parent injection. Benchmarked dedupe hashrate; currently uses 10s sliding window. Preparing canary on internal staging cluster.
notes: Implementation decisions: use W3C traceparent and a Redwood-specific message-id header. Keep the header payload minimal to avoid Kafka message size impact.

Testing plan: run E2E harness against kafka-staging with synthetic load generator, compare traces exported to tempo-staging and verify parent-child relationships using trace IDs and message-id mapping.
Rollout plan: internal services -> sandbox tenants -> opt-in beta customers -> full rollout. Monitor stitch-success-rate, orphaned-span-ratio, span-duplication-rate, p99 latency.
Follow-ups: consider integrating sampling hints from origin service so stitched spans can respect upstream sampling decisions.
